facts.statement: A twin who travels far at near light speed and comes back is younger than the twin who stayed on Earth; the travelling twin is the one who accelerates and turns around.
One g is standard gravity, 9.80665 metres per second squared (exact by definition).

source.title: CODATA Value: standard acceleration of gravity

facts.statement: Sagittarius A*, the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, is about 26,000 light-years from Earth.
The Andromeda galaxy is about 2.5 million light-years away, our Milky Way's largest galactic neighbour.

At a constant 1 g, accelerating to the midpoint and braking to a stop, the round trip to the galactic centre takes about 40 years on board and about 52,000 years on Earth; the one-way trip takes about 20 years on board and about 26,000 on Earth. The round trip to Andromeda takes about 57 years on board and about 5 million years on Earth. Computed with hyperbolic motion (constant proper acceleration).
At the midpoint of the 1 g trip to the galactic centre, the Lorentz factor is about 13,400: a clock on board runs about 13,400 times slower than one on Earth.
